# Independent audit: sparse phase products with many factors

27 October 2026. This audits the new candidate supplied by the parent and dense-algebra agent against Proposition 3.4, Definition 3.1, Lemma 4.7 and the explicit arithmetic estimates in the governing source. The result is conditional on that source. It is not a practical-speed or historical-priority claim.

## 1. Signed Boolean phase: the algebraic reduction is valid

Let P(x)=XOR_{S in M} product_{v in S} x_v be an explicitly listed polynomial over F_2, of degree at most a fixed k, on n original Boolean inputs. Repeated monomials may be cancelled modulo two and repeated powers within a monomial reduced to first powers. Put ell=n+2 and use the commutative Q-algebra

    A=Q[V]/(V^ell).

Give every monomial occurrence its own factor and its own incidence variables:

    Phi_S(Y_S)=1-2V product_{v in S} Y_(S,v).

The factor scope has size at most k. A retained product term selecting j factors has V-degree j<ell and incidence degree at most kj. Therefore the product in A has incidence degree at most

    d=k(ell-1)=k(n+1),

independently of the number m of factors. This is precisely hypothesis (3.2), including its requirement that different factor incidences be considered independent before substitutions. No global multilinearization or common replacement for all occurrences is being assumed.

At T=0 all replacement rows restore the original inputs. For Boolean x, the untruncated product evaluated at V=1 equals (-1)^P(x). Each omitted j-term is divisible by 2^j and j>=ell. Consequently, if Z_trunc is the coefficient sum of the truncated product summed over x, then

    Z_trunc = sum_x (-1)^P(x)  (mod 2^(n+2)).

The true signed sum Z lies in [-2^n,2^n]. Its residue modulo 2^(n+2) uniquely determines it, using a centered representative, and

    # {x:P(x)=0}=(2^n+Z)/2.

The n+2 precision is sufficient and avoids an actual ambiguity: modulo 2^(n+1), the two endpoint sums +2^n and -2^n coincide. Constant monomials are harmless degree-zero factors or may be extracted as a known global sign.

Evaluation at V=1 is not a well-defined algebra homomorphism on Q[V]/(V^ell). It is the specified linear coefficient-sum map on the unique degree-below-ell representative, used only after exact reconstruction at T=0. # Independent audit: arbitrary Hadamard/diagonal alternation

27 October 2026. Audited Corollary 6.1 (`cor:hadamard`) in
`deliverables/Astra_P3_Constructive_Phase_Representations.tex` and the
implementation `work_root/hadamard_phase_compiler.py`.

## Finding

The corollary is valid, conditional on the local phase-product theorem
and its governing manuscript. No normalization, path multiplicity,
locality, or original-qubit complexity gap was found. The restriction
`h_H <= C n` is essential to the claimed parameter transfer.

## Path representation

Start every wire at the constant zero. A diagonal gate changes no wire
value and contributes its phase on the current wire values. Each Hadamard
introduces exactly one fresh Boolean path variable v, replacing the old
wire value u, with kernel

    <v|H|u> = 2^(-1/2) (-1)^(u v).

The complete expression therefore has exactly h_H introduced variables
before boundary reduction, at most m+h_H phase terms, and locality at
most max(k,2). The Hadamard sign is a permitted phase because -1 is the
q/2-th power of a primitive q=2^b-th root. Constant old values only reduce
the sign to a unary phase or the constant one. Diagonal operations,
regardless of their number or alternation with Hadamards, create no path
variables.

For a requested amplitude, final wire values are pinned to the requested
computational string. Every remaining path assignment specifies one
computational history, and conversely. The amplitude is exactly

    2^(-h_H/2) times the reduced phase sum.

## Marginals and multiplicity

Multiplying an amplitude path expression by its conjugate creates two
independent copies of the path variables and changes the sign of every
phase exponent in the second copy. Pin the measured final wires in both
copies. Summing unmeasured output values imposes equality of the two final
bits on each unmeasured wire.

There is no extra factor of two from an unmeasured output: each pair of
paths with matching endpoints determines that output bit uniquely. A
constant final wire contributes one allowed endpoint, not two. Union-find
elimination of equality constraints replaces each consistent equivalence
